text:
sam: Quick sync: drafting a one-page Dedicated onboarding playbook we can hand to Sales, Solutions, and Oncall. Purpose: reduce back-and-forth, set clear acceptance gates, and codify rollback + billing mapping. Thoughts?

anya: Love it. I can own the checklist. Need clarity on forecast lead times and what constitutes a pass/fail for the smoke tests.

mike: Suggest we keep acceptance tests tiny and automatable so Sales can kick them off in staging:
- 5m steady load at expected QPS: 95th latency < target
- p99 latency within allowed degradation (configurable)
- KV/prefix cache smoke (basic correctness)
- Eviction scenario: simulate preemption and verify graceful fallback
If script exits non-zero -> fail.

sam: Good. Let's include an example script snippet in the playbook.

anya: Forecast windows: propose minimum 14d lead time for new pool provisioning (regional capacity ops). For resizing existing reserved capacity, 72h is reasonable. Document these as hard gates so Sales knows.

jordan: Ops requirements: handover checklist must include:
- PagerDuty assignment for 24h post-cutover (owner explicitly named)
- Monitoring dashboard link + runbook link
- Prewarm plan (if purchased) and how to trigger it
- Rollback/run revert steps and timings
I can add a PagerDuty template.

elaine: Billing note: Sales often promises "X burst". We need a deterministic mapping: reserved slots -> base invoice; burst SLA as billable add-on; overage pricing defined per 1M tokens or per-minute reserved throughput. Without that mapping, Finance gets tickets. I'll draft pricing language.

mike: Can we automate the smoke tests as a single runner that uploads a small HTML/JSON report to the runbook page? That makes acceptance check idempotent. We gate on script exit code + presence of report.

deploy-bot: created draft page: https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated/onboarding-playbook-v0.1 :link:

ops-bot: I'll own the 24h monitoring window for the first three pilot customers and will add a templated checklist to the PD handoff.

sam: Two policy decisions we need to resolve before shippable playbook:
1) Burst guarantees: paid opt-in SLA vs default soft best-effort?
2) Autoscale cooldowns: platform default vs per-customer tuning?

elaine: My proposal: default = soft-burst best-effort. Offer a paid burst guarantee as an opt-in add-on with clear pricing and capacity reservations. Keep contractual language simple: "Burst SLA = X sustained extra throughput for Y minutes."

jordan: For cooldowns, start with a centralized sane default (reduces ops complexity). Allow a per-customer override but only via an Ops review and with extra fees / stricter guardrails.

anya: Action items I will add to the doc:
- Forecast windows (14d new / 72h resize)
- Link to smoke test runner and expected exit codes
- PagerDuty handoff template + owner field
- Billing mapping draft (assigned to elaine)
- Policy options section (burst SLA opt-in + cooldown override workflow)

mike: Small addendum: acceptance tests should be run in staging against an isolated pool that mirrors prod config. Include a tiny k6/hey snippet in the playbook. Example:
```
# run quick latency smoke
k6 run --vus 20 --duration 5m smoke-test.js || exit 1
```

sam: Timeline: aim to pilot with 1-2 customers in 3 weeks. After pilot, iterate the playbook and bake the smoke runner into CI.

ops-bot: noted. I'll schedule the PD template and the 24h monitoring rota.

elaine: I'll sync with Finance tomorrow on how to present burst add-on on invoices.

sam: Great. Once anya pushes the checklist I'll add this to the Dedicated roadmap item and flag the two policy decisions for the leadership review next week. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
